nistCosmoSacSoftware.evidence: MIT licensed; NIST states that the software is not subject to copyright in the USA, with foreign rights reserved by the Secretary of Commerce.

evidence: Pinned upstream release binaries and local license texts are retained under vendor/.
Official release URLs, publisher archive checksums, extracted executable checksums, source commits, and local license hashes are frozen in vendor/release-provenance.json.
LGPL-3.0 permits use, modification, and redistribution under its stated conditions; BSD-3-Clause permits source/binary use and redistribution subject to notice conditions.
The generated-data admission does not rely on a right to the NIST UD/VT or ThermoSAC profile databases.
All six molecules use GFN2-xTB 6.7.1 with tight gas-phase geometry optimization and CPCM-X 1.1.0 xTB conductor surfaces at epsilon=infinity.
GFN2-xTB is a parameterized semiempirical tight-binding method and therefore has no separately selected orbital basis set.
The method is qualified for an internally consistent NIST loader/topology-gate input basis only; accuracy and LLE topology are not admitted by this record.

molecularSurfaceFiles.evidence: Six retained CPCM-X .cosmo surfaces were computed in this project from exact molecular structures without restricted profile or surface database input. Integrity hashes are frozen in generated/generation-manifest.json.

profileConversion.softwareLicense: CPCM-X LGPL-3.0 plus project-authored wrapper code
evidence: CPCM-X emits the 153-row three-part sigma profile directly; the wrapper preserves its bins and adds NIST loader metadata.
The verifier enforces the -0.025 to +0.025 e/A^2 grid, 0.001 spacing, NHB/OH/OT order, finite nonnegative bins, surface-area conservation, identity matching, and per-file hashes.
Molecular volume is frozen by deterministic 0.05 A midpoint integration of the union of CPCM-X cavity spheres retained in each surface file.

resultingProfileData.evidence: The six surfaces/profiles are newly computed project output. No UD, VT2005, ThermoSAC, LVPP, or other profile/surface database file was used as a calculation input. License notices for the generating software are retained separately.
